newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine mortgage bank sees loans rising 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Argentine mortgage bank sees loans rising 40 pct.

text.p: Argentina's state-owned National Mortgage Bank (BHN) plans to grant $1.2 billion in housing loans in 1997, a 40 percent rise on last year, BHN president Pablo Rojo said Friday.

"In 1997 we hope to keep growing at a strong pace to reach more or less 1.2 billion pesos in credit disbursements, which means a monthly rate of 100 million pesos which we hadn't achieved for a long time," Rojo told a local radio.
In separate statements to the daily Clarin, Rojo said the bank would issue debt worth $650 million this year through normal and mortgage-backed bonds, compared to $450 million in 1996.
Rojo estimated the bank would grant 40,000 individual loans in 1997 and would finance a program to build 36,000 housing units, of which 12,000 would be finished this year.

"Our interest rates for loans in the mortgage sector are getting more and more similar to European ones, our loan durations are long, and our construction sector has been showing very strong signs of recovery in the past three months," Rojo told the radio interviewer.
He said the BHN currently lends to retail banks funds at 11 percent and blamed these high rates on domestic taxes and steep fees for notary publics and real estate agencies.
Rojo also denied mortgage loans were being beefed up as a way of helping the ruling Peronist party win this year's midterm elections.

"Ever since the bank turned into a wholesaler there is no chance (of using funds for electioneering), because the one who grants the credits, screens clients and is in charge of collecting loan payments is a private bank," said Rojo.

He noted past political control of bank funds had placed it on the brink of bankruptcy in 1989, but said this was averted a year later by President Carlos Menem's decision to reform it and make it a wholesale bank.
